title.narrative: Leading the Charge to Eradicate Rural Poverty

description.narrative: Nigeria is our newest country of operation, and is already showing significant indicators of rapid growth and deep farmer impact. As a result, we plan to accelerate this growth over the next few years, with the goal of serving 1 million farmers by 2030 through all impact channels. We currently operate our traditional core program, a tree-planting platform, nascent rural retail channel, and crop buy-back trials.

Our prior project with the Dutch Government, “Subsistence to Self-Reliance – Bringing the Power of Markets to Africa’s Lowest-Income Farmers” underscored our shared passion for inclusive economic development and showcased the key milestones that we can accomplish together. Core operating support from DGIS facilitated the strategic expansion of One Acre Fund’s ‘impact ecosystem.’ Within two years, we doubled the scale of our farmer network, launched operations in two new country programs (Malawi and Uganda), and rolled out impactful new products like tree planting kits and clean cookstoves at country-wide scale. Simultaneously, we refined our innovative systems-change platform, leveraging our core organizational competencies to improve large-scale public and private actors’ service to smallholders. This success has now placed One Acre Fund in a position where we can realistically envision moving the needle on hunger and poverty across the entire African continent. Our current project with DGIS, “Leading the Charge to Eradicate Rural Poverty,” aims to capture this powerful opportunity. The project involves a smartly structured two-part investment spanning September 15, 2018 – December 31, 2022: First, DGIS is once again providing critical support to the varied, evolving platforms within our organization that lay the foundation for our growth and impact. Core operating support from DGIS will enhance and extend One Acre Fund’s proven model by funding key strategic priorities across our M&E, R&D, and new country expansion units. Secondly, DGIS is also providing working capital to revolutionize One Acre Fund’s growth trajectory. This injection to our ‘permanent fund’ will completely fund our projected expansion of 245,000+ new farm families in 2019, bringing us past the 1 millionth farmer milestone. Crucially, farmers’ loan repayments will replenish our permanent fund each year, allowing us to re-extend this contribution to provide input loans to an estimated 245,000 farm families (including over 980,000 children) annually. This project will anchor One Acre Fund’s expansion to directly serve 1.85 million farm families annually by year-end 2022. Simultaneously, it will help us reach an additional 3.5 million farmers via systems-change partnerships that are expressly designed to transform entire agricultural ecosystems. Together, the reach of these efforts will generate transformative change for rural communities across rural Africa.

title.narrative: One Acre Fund's key cost-effectiveness measure.

comment.narrative: In response to the large number of groups that failed to complete their repayment in previous years, we set out to improve repayment in 2020 by pegging our repayment pushes to mid-year harvests such as melons, when farmers are likely to have cash on hand. We also worked to promote group cohesion and provided additional guidance on group formation during the enrollment process. Note that our Nigeria program, still in the pilot stage, does not yet benefit from the economies of scale and operational efficiencies of our larger programs. As such, we achieved an SROI of 0.5.

We measure our efficiency, or Social Return On Investment (SROI), as the amount of new profits our farmers generate for every $1 of donor investment in our program. SROI from our Nigeria program was well above target. For impact, as mentioned above, we achieved above-target results. For costs, revenues were largely in line with expectations thanks to robust loan repayment (96% vs 94% target), a strong sign of farmer demand for and satisfaction with our program. Program spending was similarly in line with budget.

We project that every $1 donated towards our program will generate $8.30 in impact this year. This is slightly higher than the target we set for our program at the beginning of 2022. Performance in this area was driven by strong impact (as above), alongside robust site economics that drove down our cost to serve. That included very high loan repayment of 98%, among the highest at the organization, as well as a high ratio of clients per field officer (500+ vs ~200 in Kenya).

title.narrative: Farm families participating in One Acre Fund's core program.

comment.narrative: Despite COVID-19 related disruptions, we nearly quadrupled the number of farmers we serve in 2021, reaching 8,863 families. To continue scaling at this rate, we are committed to innovating technological tools to drive operational efficiencies, generating consistent impact, and building the underlying systems to accommodate rapid future scale. As the pilot is on track to achieve positive site economics, we anticipate unlocking a sharper growth trajectory in subsequent seasons.

In 2020, we had strong enrollment despite major disruptions from COVID-19, enrolling 1,800 farmers - more than double the clients from 2019 (800). We credit several factors for driving increased enrollment this year, including our growing presence in our areas of operation, strong harvests last year, field officer recruitment initiatives, and the introduction of a new, high-demand cash crop (yams). In addition, in early 2020 we received positive reception from village leaders — many of whom used to be skeptical of our program due to past experiences with fraudulent organizations — which undoubtedly drove demand for our program. An additional factor in our ability to scale has been increasing visibility and credibility with our government partners e.g. we built strong relations with high-ranking government officials in Niger State, including two members of the Niger State’s cabinet and the Director-General of the state coordinating agency for Commodities and Export Promotion.

We served 24,100 clients through our core program in 2022, nearly tripling in size in a single year. Our key value proposition in Nigeria is the provision of high-quality inputs on credit, coupled with flexible training, which is driving robust demand for our program. A further driver of demand includes a positive client experience, which helps with client retention and supports our marketing efforts. Lastly, strong senior Nigerian leadership and the country’s large population of rural farm families place us on a realistic track for rapid future growth.

title.narrative: The profit boost achieved by farming with One Acre Fund.

comment.narrative: Our ability to implement our core program despite COVID-19 restrictions ensured that farmers boosted their incomes substantially on the activities we support. The impact from yams, a cash crop on offer for the first time in 2020, further contributed to strong impact for our clients.

We achieved an impact of $298 in Nigeria in 2021, well above our target of $180. This was our highest organization-wide impact for 2021. Primary factors included strong maize harvest improvements over control farmers (43%) and high crop selling prices. Looking ahead, we are deepening our commitment to crop diversification to ensure our farmers are food secure.

We will report our final 2022 impact figure in early 2023, but preliminary analysis shows that we may fall just short of the ambitious impact target we set for 2022. Still, Nigeria remains on track to be our highest impact-generating program country, driven by larger average land sizes. Key drivers of financial impact in 2022 included our diverse crop offerings (including higher-revenue varieties such as yams and groundnuts), and promising buy-back trials for maize and groundnuts which increased farmer profits.

title.narrative: Farm families reached through systems-change unit.

comment.narrative: We define farm families 'reached' as households that benefitted from at least one systems-change intervention. Our systems-change unit is currently investigating partnership opportunities to expand beyond our core program in Nigeria. In particular, we are dedicated to strengthening our pilot agroforestry model. We are also in talks on a partnership with the government to expand our platform in the near future.
We did not implement any systems-change programs in Nigeria in 2020, instead focusing on our growing our core program and improving operational performance.

We created impact through two channels in 2022: tree distribution and a recently launched rural retail program. For trees, we distributed 700,000 seedlings to 56,000 farmers. Our model focuses on seedling production via entrepreneur-owned community nurseries, which produce seedlings cost-effectively and reduce transport costs. For retail, we served 1,300 farmers in 2022 and generated revenue of $800,000, well above our projections. In 2023, we aim to scale while fine-tuning our approach, with the vision of scaling aggressively thereafter to improve farmer access to high-quality inputs.
